question: Which nested NAE families have no allowed state at some finite depth while the bottomless pattern lives, how often, and does the largest self-consistent relation inside the knot decide life at every depth?

definitions.E: every one-definition family with 3 ports, 0-3 own distinctions, 1-3 distinct calls (knots unordered, SELF ordered, at least one SELF).
definitions.W: families drawn by SHORT-DESC's code (main variant), 8 workers x 150,000 tries, seeds sha256 LO:worker.
definitions.limit: greatest fixed point from 'nothing'; lives iff main relation non-empty there (compactness).
definitions.L2: alive at every depth iff main(P) non-empty, P the largest tuple inside the knot with P inside Phi(P).

public_inputs.code: census.py (sha256 0d5328a27d2fd7429c4bcb80228d440bef2edd2cd526ef91aad5003405ee35bc) beside this file; SHORT-DESC dlang.py; numpy.
public_inputs.run: census.py --exhaustive W 8 for W in 0-7 and --sample W 150000 for W in 0-7, then --summary, from the repository root; output artifacts/LIMIT-ONLY-20261112-001A/LIMIT-ONLY-20261112-001A-E001_limit_only/.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the classes, criteria, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
primary_observable: Counts by comparability, fate and limit; L2 failures; the share of 'down' among families alive only in the limit.
cheapest_meaningful_control: The proved gates (L1; L2 where knot and image compare).
validation_gate: G1: L1 no exception; L2 no failure where knot and image compare.

predictions.P2: at least one L2 failure in W
predictions.P3: share down among limit-only >= 0.5 in E and in W
predictions.P4: W: share of finitely dying families alive in the limit >= 0.5

stop_rule: One run and its summary; a hand-off to the referee thread; report.
